name: Teaspoon
funFact: The teaspoon was standardised at 4.93 ml in the US in 1893 — but a 'teaspoon' in recipes from the 1800s could mean anything from 2 to 6 ml.

name: Can of soda
funFact: The 355 ml (12 fl oz) can size was standardised in the US in 1953 — it was chosen to match the volume of a standard serving glass at the time.

name: Wine bottle
funFact: The 750 ml bottle was standardised partly because it matched the lung capacity of a glassblower — the original bottles were literally blown by human breath.

name: Bathtub
funFact: A full bathtub uses more water than a 10-minute shower — the average bath uses 150–300 litres while a low-flow showerhead uses about 8 litres per minute.

name: Olympic pool
funFact: An Olympic pool holds 2.5 million litres — if you drank 2 litres of water per day it would take you 3,424 years to drink the whole pool.

name: Human stomach
funFact: An empty stomach is about the size of a fist — but can expand to hold up to 4 litres when fully stretched, though 1 litre is comfortable.

name: Hot tub
funFact: A hot tub at 40°C loses about 3% of its water per week to evaporation — and you need to replace chemicals every time it rains.

name: Car fuel tank
funFact: The average petrol car tank holds about 55 litres — enough to drive roughly 700 km, or about the distance from London to Edinburgh and back.

name: Human blood volume
description: Total blood in an adult human ≈ 5 litres.
funFact: Your body circulates its entire blood supply roughly once per minute — the heart pumps about 5 litres per minute at rest.

name: Milk carton
funFact: The paperboard milk carton was invented in 1915 but only became widespread in the 1950s — before that, milk was delivered in glass bottles that you'd return for a deposit.

name: Earth's oceans
description: Total volume of Earth's oceans ≈ 1.335 × 10²¹ litres.
funFact: If you compressed all of Earth's ocean water into a sphere, it would be about 1,385 km in diameter — smaller than the Moon.

name: Teardrop
funFact: A human tear is about 6.5 microlitres. Emotional tears contain different proteins than reflex tears (from dust or onions) — specifically higher concentrations of stress hormones, which may be why crying actually reduces stress levels.

name: Eye drop
funFact: The human eye can only hold about 30 microlitres of fluid — meaning roughly 40% of every eye drop immediately overflows down the tear duct. Pharmaceutical companies know this but still make standard drops 50 microlitres, since a too-small drop is worse than an overflow.

name: Shot glass
funFact: Shot glass sizes vary wildly by country — a US shot is 44ml, a UK single is 25ml, a Japanese 'ichigo' is 60ml. The origin of the word 'shot' is disputed, but a popular theory links it to frontier America, where a single bullet was supposedly traded for a measure of whiskey.

name: Pint
exampleMeme: The unit of a good evening.
funFact: A UK pint is 568ml, a US pint is 473ml — a difference that has created genuine confusion in pub-heavy cities like New York. The UK pint is larger because it's based on the imperial gallon; the US gallon comes from an older 'Queen Anne' gallon of 1707, before the British standardised upward.

name: Human lung capacity
exampleMeme: Everything in your lungs right now.
funFact: Your lungs hold about 6 litres at maximum capacity, but you only use about 0.5 litres in a normal breath. Professional free divers train their lungs to expand beyond 10 litres and can hold their breath for over 20 minutes by slowing their heart rate to fewer than 20 beats per minute.

name: Wheelie bin
funFact: The standard 240-litre wheelie bin was adopted across the UK and Australia in the 1980s after studies showed it reduced back injuries in refuse collectors by 75% compared to manually lifting bags. Before wheeled bins, rubbish collection was among the most injury-prone jobs in local government.

name: Garden hose (1 minute)
description: Standard garden hose flow rate ≈ 15 litres per minute.
funFact: A garden hose running for 10 minutes uses as much water as the average person drinks in 6 weeks. A standard lawn requires roughly 25mm of water per week — calculating this precisely with a hose is nearly impossible, which is why most lawns are either drowned or parched.

name: Shipping container
funFact: There are approximately 17 million shipping containers in the world, with around 6 million in active transit at any given time. The standardisation of container sizes in the 1950s by Malcolm McLean reduced shipping costs by 97%, enabling the modern global economy.

name: Hot air balloon
description: Standard hot air balloon envelope ≈ 2,800 m³ (2,800,000 litres).
funFact: A hot air balloon envelope holds roughly 2,800 cubic metres of air heated to 100°C. The heated air is only about 25% less dense than the surrounding atmosphere — yet this difference in density is enough to lift the basket, burner, fuel tanks, and passengers. The entire flight is engineered around a density difference smaller than the margin of error on most scales.

name: Great Barrier Reef
description: Volume of water over the Great Barrier Reef ≈ 152 trillion litres.
funFact: The Great Barrier Reef is visible from space and is the world's largest living structure — built by organisms so small you need a microscope to see them individually. It has taken 500,000 years to reach its current size and produces 50% of the oxygen in the area it covers.
